title: On‑Prem Subscription & SLA Flex Model: pricing experiments, upgrade cadence, and enterprise contract needs
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: Design and run pricing/packaging experiments for Private/VPC and on‑prem deliveries covering license fee structures, support tiers, and upgrade cadences that map to procurement and security questionnaire requirements.

Background: Sales and Solutions have signaled frequent pushback on fixed annual license fees for on‑prem customers where hardware heterogeneity and procurement cycles vary widely. Legal & Security require contract language and SLAs that mirror the hosted product but must support private controls (KMS/HSM, data residency, audit logs). Our objective is to identify 2–3 experimentally validated packaging options that balance predictable revenue (ARR/ACV) with win rates on RFPs and acceptable operational cost for Redwood.

Hypotheses to test:
- H1: A hybrid pricing anchor (low annual license + per‑node perpetual maintenance or a usage floor) increases mid‑market conversion by 15% vs. straight list license.
- H2: Offering 3 support tiers (Standard: business hours, Business: 24x5, Enterprise: 24x7 with named POA) will improve NRR on Private deals by reducing churn on installs with higher SLO needs.
- H3: A 6‑month major upgrade cadence + quarterly security patches reduces professional services lift and is preferred by enterprise legal vs. annual major + ad‑hoc patches.

Proposed packaging variants (for experiments):
1) Subscription + Capacity Credits: Low fixed subscription (covers control plane & support), capacity credits for reserved GPU pools priced per capacity unit. Annual billing with multi‑year discounts.
2) Perpetual License + Annual Maintenance: Higher one‑time license fee amortized over 3 years in quoting, plus annual maintenance (25%) for support and upgrades. Optional managed upgrade add‑on.
3) Term License w/ Flexible Upgrade Window: 12/24/36 month term options with included regular minor/patch updates; major upgrades optional, billed as bundle or on demand.

Support tiers and mapping (draft):
- Standard: Business hours support, 2 business day response, community access, general upgrades.
- Business: 24x5 support, 4 hour response for Sev1, quarterly review, runbook access.
- Enterprise: 24x7 with SLA credits, named technical account manager, onsite/boarding credits, guaranteed upgrade windows, and accelerated vulnerability fixes.

Upgrade cadence tradeoffs:
- Faster cadence reduces long tail maintenance and security exposure but increases upgrade orchestration work for customers (and requires more migration tooling).
- Slower cadence reduces customer operational churn but increases patch surface and contractual complexity for security attestations.

Contract & security questionnaire alignment:
- Must include: data handling, KMS/HSM integration options, audit log retention, vulnerability disclosure process, agreed maintenance & patching SLAs, incident escalation path, and breach notification timelines.
- Work with Legal to standardize modular contract exhibits for: (a) Managed Upgrades, (b) Air‑gapped deployments, (c) HSM/KMS addendum, (d) SLA credits calculation formula.

Signals & success metrics:
- Primary: Win rate on RFPs for Private/VPC deals, ACV / ARR for on‑prem customers.
- Secondary: Deal velocity (proposal→signed), churn within 12 months, number of contract exceptions requested, PS hours for upgrade assistance.

Experiment plan (next 8 weeks):
- Week 1–2: Draft pricing sheets and contract exhibits; align with Legal, Security, Finance.
- Week 3–4: Pilot 3 price packages with 3 active prospects (one enterprise in fintech, one mid‑market SaaS, one regulated healthcare). Capture responses and procurement objections.
- Week 5–6: Iterate with Sales on anchor messaging and quote templates. Track changes in win probability and discounting.
- Week 7–8: Review outcomes and decide on GA packaging (one primary SKU + two optional addons) and the standard upgrade cadence for general availability.

Operational impacts and implementation notes: 
- Billing & Invoicing: Finance needs SKU definitions for capacity credits and multi‑year amortized invoicing.
- Entitlement & Console: Console must show installed version, last patch, allowed upgrade windows, and entitlement bucket (credits).
- Telemetry: Add flags to track enablement type (on‑prem vs private) and support tier to measure SLO adherence and PS consumption.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve: 
- Should we require a minimum capacity commitment (to avoid tiny deployments that are expensive to support) or allow low‑commit pilots at higher per‑unit prices?
- How do we surface upgrade compatibility matrices for customers with heavily customized infra?
- Pricing for air‑gapped/on‑appliance scenarios where remote telemetry is limited.

Next steps / owners: 
- PM (Nora): finalize pricing experiment plan and produce quote templates (by 2026‑03‑18).
- Legal (Ben Cho): draft modular contract exhibits and SLA credit formula (by 2026‑03‑25).
- Security (Priya Rao): produce standard answers for security questionnaire sections that map to each support/upgrade cadence (by 2026‑03‑24).
- Sales Engineering (Diego Martinez): identify pilot accounts and run initial technical win conversations (ongoing).

Longer term considerations:
- Explore an amortized, usage‑based metric tied to model tokens served or capacity utilization to align long term economics with Redwood's hosted model.
- Consider a "sustained usage" discount for customers that consolidate multiple teams onto Dedicated pools.
